# Plate tectonics: concept formation and a discriminating test {#sec-session-04}

**Meeting 4 | Tuesday, September 29, 2026 | 1:00-2:00 PM Pacific**

## Central question

How does a new concept make old observations and new measurements jointly discriminating?

## The paper pair

**Pairing type:** Conceptual synthesis / observational test.

### Paper A: A New Class of Faults and their Bearing on Continental Drift

@wilson1965. **Nature (1965).** [Paper / publisher record](https://doi.org/10.1038/207343a0)

Read Wilson in full; sketch the competing slip-direction predictions.

*Access: Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.*

### Paper B: Mechanism of earthquakes and nature of faulting on the mid-oceanic ridges

@sykes1967. **Journal of Geophysical Research (1967).** [Paper / publisher record](https://doi.org/10.1029/JZ072i008p02131)

Read Sykes’ abstract, focal-mechanism evidence relevant to transform faults, and conclusions.

*Access: Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.*

### Why these papers belong together

Wilson’s transform-fault concept enables a specific observational contrast. Sykes uses earthquake mechanisms to examine faulting on oceanic ridges. This is a positive case for hypothesis testing, enabled by concepts and measurement systems that did not arrive from a simple automated loop. [@wilson1965; @sykes1967]

## Prepare before the meeting

Bring an annotated sketch of a ridge-offset geometry and two possible causal interpretations.

## Discussion questions

1. What was the new conceptual object, not merely the new dataset?
2. Which result could have counted against the predicted fault motion?
3. What can these two papers establish about tectonics, and what larger history do they omit?

## One-hour meeting

| Time | Activity |
|:--|:--|
| 0-10 min | Independent first judgments; surface disagreements. |
| 10-25 min | Compare the papers: claim, evidence, assumptions, and limits. |
| 25-45 min | Work through the case exercise below. |
| 45-55 min | Translate the discussion into agent requirements and tests. |
| 55-60 min | Record an output and one unresolved disagreement. |

### Case exercise

Build the wider plate-tectonics evidence graph, labeling surveys, instrument advances, models, and tests. Then isolate the Wilson-Sykes link and reconstruct the discriminating prediction without using later consensus as its proof.

## Agent-design or evaluation output

Synthesis-agent specification: preserve provenance across datasets, identify shared implications, and state a prediction that separates explanations.

## Record after the meeting

Record the evidence for your main claim, what changed your mind, what remains unresolved, and one change to the agent or its evaluation. Keep confidential examples in private group notes rather than committing them to this public book.
